title: Harness history event
description: One row of the one history (epic #59): today's event envelope plus where the row came from (provenance). Every row from every era (main, dogfood, dogfood2, sessions, GitHub, the live runtime) has this shape. A field that could not be recovered holds a legacy placeholder, never an invented value, and provenance.placeholders lists its path. Rows are never edited: a format change adds an event version and a declared conversion. src/history.js reads this file; nothing restates it.

schemaVersion.description: The history schema the row was written in (schemaVersion above). A row without one was written before the field and is at absentMeans. A page that reads the history declares the range it reads (pages/<page>/needs.json, reads.schemaVersion) and, on a history with a row outside it, shows a red banner naming the mismatch and no data.

id.description: The event id as its source wrote it. Ids are unique within one source, not across sources (dogfood and dogfood2 share orchestrator ids).

version.description: The row's position in the one history, counted from 1 in time order.

to.description: The machine address the event went to (harness, budget, item:<id>, item:<id>/decision:<...>).

relayedBy.description: The session that relayed a tap or message (harness meta.sources).

harness.description: The harness that applied (or, for a recovered row, would have applied) the event.

route.description: The route the event took when it was written: the ids of the routes ("route" in the machine JSON) its transitions took, in order. Replay takes this route (harness meta.store.facts). A row written before routes were recorded has none.

v.description: The event type's version (events below). Absent means 1.

legacy.description: Why the value is missing, e.g. 'main predates the envelope (M1)'.
A placeholder for a value that could not be recovered.

actor.description: Who sent the event. The kinds and id forms are harness meta.actors.

source.description: Where the event came from. The kinds are harness meta.sources.

ref.description: A path under harness/archive/ (or the live store's name), as C1 lays it out.

line.description: The line (JSONL) or event index the row was read from.

origin.description: live: the runtime wrote it into this history. migrated: copied from an older store, upcast. recovered: reconstructed from a session transcript, GitHub or the Library, where no store recorded it.

also.description: Other sources that described the same fact (identity below); the merger keeps them here.

placeholders.description: Paths in this row (actor, harness, event.sha, ...) that hold a legacy placeholder. Exactly those, no more and no fewer.

confidence.description: Only on a recovered row where reading the source took judgement; the from line points at the evidence.

events.description: Every event type the history holds, with its current version and the payload fields it needs to mean anything (a weak schema: the rest are optional, because eras differ). Every type the machines take is here; OUT_OF_BAND, which records work done outside the gates, the item takes as a fact. A version above 1 needs a declared conversion from each earlier one. Every field a page reads (pages/<page>/needs.json) is a property here, in the envelope or in its type's schema, so dropping one fails naming the page and the field.

OUT_OF_BAND.description: Work done outside the gates on someone's order (a merge by hand on the person's say-so, #46 and #52). It is history, never a reason for a new store: who ordered it, the message that did, what was done, which gates or states were skipped and the PR it touched (pr). A landing also names the head that landed (sha). A session sends it to the item with harness send, in any state of the item, done and cancelled included: the item takes it as a fact (workItem on.OUT_OF_BAND, harness meta.store records), its state unchanged. harness doctor lists every one, and does not count a landing one records as a problem (harness meta.invariants reviewOnHead). An order given by no chat message (a button pressed on GitHub) holds a legacy placeholder in message.

identity.description: How the merger knows two rows describe one fact (C4). The first rule whose types include the row's type gives its key: the values at the listed paths, joined. A row missing any key path keeps a key of its own and is never merged. Of rows with one key, the one whose provenance.from.source is the rule's owner is kept (else the earliest), and the others' from go to its provenance.also. Rows with one key that disagree on a payload field both have are a conflict the merger reports, never merges silently. Two rows of one source (provenance.from.ref) are never one fact: a source records a fact once, so the second row of a key in one source is that key's second fact (a stand-in's answer and its re-ask under a grant share a decision address), and the n-th of one source is one fact only with the n-th of another, in time order.

rules.why: A PR merges once; GitHub owns that fact.
CI on one head of one PR; GitHub owns it.
An item id is filed once.
The decision address is item + class + attempt; the store owns machine decisions.
One Agent tool call is one spawn.
The order is a message the session read.

otherwise.why: Any other row is its own fact within its source.

steps.description: What each row of a history did, beside it in steps.jsonl: one step per row, in the history's order, joined to its row by version (and id). harness replay --steps writes it by replaying the history with the current code, each row a fact (harness meta.store.facts), and reads it off its scratch copy before and after each row: the actors whose state the row changed, the context fields it changed, the effects it queued with the acks the store holds for them, and its route. A row replay cannot apply is a step with the reason (refused) and no changes. A page that reads it (pages/<page>/needs.json reads.with) declares the fields it reads here, so dropping one fails naming the page and the field.

version.description: The history row this step is.

refused.description: Why replay could not apply the row (a second row of an id it applied already is one: replay applies an id once); null when it applied it.

route.description: The ids of the routes the row took on replay; null when it was refused.

actors.description: Each actor whose state the row changed: its address (harness, item:<id>, item:<id>/<child id>) and its state before and after, as text (null: the actor was not there).

context.description: Each context field the row changed: the actor's address, the field, and its value before and after (null: absent).

effects.description: Each effect the row queued (id, name, subject) and the acks the store holds for it, oldest first (none: pending, or a store that keeps no acks, as a joined history).
